record.original_question: Define Otto conjugacy on a semigroup S by a ∼o b if there exist elements u and v in S such that au = ub and va = bv. Is there a finite semigroup S for which ∼o is a congruence and the quotient semigroup S/∼o is not cancellative?

evidence.quote: We define such an example that has infinite size and we leave as an open question whether a finite example exists.
Problem 9.4. Is there a finite semigroup for which ∼o is a congruence and S/ ∼o is not cancelative?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a semigroup. Define the Otto conjugacy relation $\sim_o$ on $S$ by declaring $a \sim_o b$ if and only if there exist elements $u, v \in S$ such that
$$au = ub \quad \text{and} \quad va = bv.$$
A semigroup $T$ is said to be cancellative if for all $x, y, z \in T$, both $xy = xz \Rightarrow y = z$ and $yx = zx \Rightarrow y = z$.

Determine whether there exists a finite semigroup $S$ such that:
(i) $\sim_o$ is a congruence on $S$ (i.e., an equivalence relation compatible with multiplication on both sides), and
(ii) the quotient semigroup $S/\!\sim_o$ is not cancellative.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question, with an infinite example known but no finite example established. A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent resolution producing or excluding a finite witness, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On three approaches to conjugacy in semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style discussion of conjugacy notions in semigroups including the Otto-style relation, without reporting a finite noncancellative quotient example.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the finite case for Otto conjugacy quotient cancellativity is reported in the related literature surfaced by search.

status_evidence.title: Conjugacy in Semigroups (Araújo et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses several conjugacy relations on semigroups and their congruence properties.
status_evidence.claim: Background source on semigroup conjugacy notions; does not provide a finite example resolving the question.
